DECISION: YES. EV-MONO-1ef611 needs independent review before it becomes official, meaning before any decision may rely on it as evidence. That review is CU-7: a fresh rule-12 review-breakthrough at max effort, in an independent session, of the cured route-(c) object. This is recorded as a precondition on reliance and on the successor batch. It is not added as a card, because no identifiers were issued for one. Reasons. (1) AGENTS.md core rule 12 binds 'any claim proposed as a ... closure result'. The sole function of this record is to supply the datum that the closure gate requires before route (c) can close a lane (agents/coordinator.md 'Closure gate'; J3 G-2). It is therefore part of a proposed closure result. (2) AGENTS.md 'Review architecture' defines claim-changing as able to 'move a hypothesis status, close a lane, or support a headline claim'. On its own the record moves nothing. But it is the evidence that a lane closure must cite, so it is claim-relevant in the sense of agents/coordinator.md 'Dynamic dispatch'. That section requires an independent reviewer before 'the Coordinator records the official decision'. (3) Amendment A01 decides this case expressly. Under K4c, J1's composed B-W (SC-2) 'is cured only when the corrected statement is carried verbatim as the scope of a committed record that the adopting decision cites, and that record has been reviewed by a fresh rule-12 review'. Under K1e, the J2 and J3 DISSENTs persist until a decision cites 'a fresh rule-12 review of the cured object'. Without CU-7, this record cures nothing. (4) It differs from CU-5. The BATCH-8609e2 assessment exempted CORR-20261005-a53ac8 because that correction withdrew an unverified directive: it reopened rather than closed, and it added no claim. This record does the opposite. It asserts a derivation-level obstruction in favour of closure. It carries the SC-2 wording, which no review has yet examined as the scope of a record, because the reviewer wrote it and A01 placed it outside the pre-registered carve-out. And it carries a Coordinator-authored resource_check reading that has never been attacked. Every one of those is new, unreviewed, claim-bearing content. (5) Review does NOT come before archiving. docs/claims-and-verification.md requires the refutation artifact to be 'produced and archived (snapshot commit) before the decision record that relies on it'. AGENTS.md 'Durable research commits' puts the snapshot commit 'before an independent agent reviews them'. CU-7 must also review committed bytes. So the order is: this batch's SNAPSHOT archive (c96883), then CU-7 in a successor batch, then a post-review ledger archive that binds CU-7's report and the composing decision. Only that last archive makes the record official evidence. CONSEQUENCES, written into the cards: the record states that it is unreviewed as a record (768ae1 EC-11); c96883 refuses to stage it if it asserts that any DISSENT is lifted, that B-W is cured, that the closure gate is met or that a criterion is met (EA-6); and the CU-7 review plan must list EV-MONO-1ef611 and CORR-20261005-a53ac8 as the cured object (A01 K5c). That last point is a successor duty recorded in the shard, not a second next action.

TOOL GAP 1, and the deviation it forces. agents/coordinator.md says a claim-relevant producer 'must set review_required: true and have a dependent Reviewer, Validator, or Red Team task'. tools/research_dispatch.py _validate_review_chains enforces that only inside a single queue: the reviewer must depend on the snapshot archive, and one kind:ledger archive must follow every review. CU-7 lives in a successor batch, and no reviewer or ledger-archive identifier was issued here, so a queue marking 768ae1 review_required true would not render. 768ae1 therefore carries review_required FALSE as a DISPATCHER FIELD ONLY. Its review_required_note states that the program-level requirement is not waived, and (notes: review_requirement_assessment) the requirement is carried as a precondition on reliance. This is a declared deviation from the literal text of agents/coordinator.md. Option (a) would restore the literal form: the top-level session mints a CU-7 reviewer TASK-*, a post-review ledger-archive TASK-* and a DEC-* now, and a card_revision appends them as queued tasks that depend on c96883. That option is not taken here, because CU-7 needs a complete review_plan written before its reviewer launches (A01 K5b/K5c), and that is a separate Coordinator act. ARCHIVE KIND: c96883 is kind 'snapshot' with binding_mode 'commit'. This time the label is accurate on its own terms: the record is archived BEFORE its independent review. In BATCH-8609e2, by contrast, the snapshot label was a workaround. TOOL GAP 2, for the successor: _validate_ledger_archive refuses a kind:ledger archive that names an EV-* record_id without owning a ledger/evidence/ path. Under binding_mode commit, that archive's commit must change every owned path, and EV-MONO-1ef611 will already be committed and must never change. The post-CU-7 ledger archive must therefore EITHER own the EV path under binding_mode content_first (the record is terminal, so that mode fits) OR leave the EV-* id out of record_ids and cite it from the decision. Whoever designs that card must choose one. Neither choice is made here.
